title: Haqdaar. Claim your relief payment by voice, in Urdu. A prototype, with synthetic data.
claim: Zainab is a widow who cannot read forms. She signs in with one tap, and every option on her home screen is a picture that speaks. To claim, she taps the microphone and simply talks, in Urdu. Real speech recognition and a language model pull out her name, district, household and I D number. The app asks only for what is missing, then reads everything back, and she answers yes or no. She can scan her I D card, which is checked on our own server. Nothing is ticked for her: she chooses what we may check. And the A I never approves or rejects. A rule engine decides, and when it is not sure, an officer does.
scamask: Fake relief messages are everywhere. She pastes one in, and Haqdaar says: scam, with the reasons, in words she can hear. Genuine messages carry a Haqdaar Seal that breaks if one character changes. And when she asks who can claim, the answer comes only from the published policy, with its sources.
officer: Officer Sana opens the queue. Each case comes with A I notes, the fraud signals, the exact rule version, and the confidence against the threshold. The A I explains; the human decides. Even then, money does not move: a second officer has to release every payment.
receipt: Back on her phone, Zainab hears the decision, and her Haq Receipt reads out the exact amount, so no middleman can keep a share. She can take her consent back at any time.
admin: For the administrator, rules are data, not code. The auto approve threshold is backed by real cost numbers, and the Digital Twin replays past claims to show what a rule change would do before it goes live. One switch kills the A I: every claim then goes to a person, and the service keeps running. The Scam Map shows where fake messages are being reported. The evaluation page shows measured accuracy, not promises. Team management and A P I docs make it a service other programs can use. And in Judge Mode, anyone can try to break it.
auditor: The auditor sees every step in an append only log, where each entry is hashed with the one before. One click verifies that nothing was changed.
helper: No smartphone? A trusted shopkeeper can help in Helper Mode. He needs the family's own PIN, and a banner always shows who he is acting for.
end: Haqdaar. The A I, the rules and the audit trail are real. Identity, payments and S M S are simulated. Try it live.
